Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates extensive, dense calcification outlining the cardiac silhouette, particularly along the anterior and inferior borders corresponding to the right ventricle and atrioventricular grooves. This "eggshell" calcification pattern is pathognomonic for constrictive calcified pericarditis, which can clinically present with murmurs due to altered hemodynamics or concurrent valvular pathology.
